front: State the governing rule for a separately purchased patent is initially measured at:
back: cost including directly attributable preparation costs. Purchased intangibles are initially recognized at directly attributable cost.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Explain the analytical implication of under IFRS, expenditures in the research phase are:
back: expensed as incurred. IFRS requires research expenditure to be expensed.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Resolve this long-term-asset review point: under IFRS, development expenditure is capitalized:
back: prospectively after all recognition criteria are demonstrated. Qualifying development costs are capitalized only from the recognition date.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: State the governing rule for uS GAAP generally treats research and development costs by:
back: expensing them, subject to specified software exceptions. General US GAAP treatment is expense, with software exceptions.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Explain the analytical implication of software to be sold under US GAAP is capitalized after:
back: technological feasibility is established. Technological feasibility is the relevant threshold.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Resolve this long-term-asset review point: an identifiable intangible acquired in a business combination is recognized at:
back: fair value separately from goodwill. Acquisition accounting recognizes identifiable intangibles at fair value.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: State the governing rule for consideration is 900 and identifiable net assets are 760. Goodwill is:
back: 140. Goodwill is the residual 900 − 760.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Explain the analytical implication of a finite-life intangible is generally:
back: amortized and tested when impairment indicators exist. Finite-life assets are allocated over useful life and tested on indication.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Resolve this long-term-asset review point: an indefinite-life intangible is:
back: not amortized but tested at least annually for impairment. Indefinite-life classification replaces amortization with annual testing.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: State the governing rule for capitalizing rather than expensing a qualifying cost initially produces:
back: higher assets and profit. Capitalization defers expense and records an asset.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Explain the analytical implication of compared with capitalization, immediate expensing generally produces higher:
back: later-period profit after the initial period, all else equal. Expensing avoids later amortization or depreciation.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Resolve this long-term-asset review point: internally generated brands are generally not recognized because:
back: their cost cannot be distinguished reliably from developing the business overall. Recognition and reliable-measurement constraints prevent capitalization.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: State the governing rule for training expenditure related to a new patent is most likely:
back: expensed. Training does not prepare the patent itself for intended use.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Explain the analytical implication of a development project meets IFRS criteria halfway through the year. Earlier expenditure is:
back: not reinstated as an asset. Capitalization is prospective from the recognition date.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: Resolve this long-term-asset review point: the useful life classification of an indefinite-life intangible should be:
back: reassessed each reporting period. Indefinite means no foreseeable limit and requires reassessment.
officialLearningOutcome: compare the financial reporting of the following types of intangible assets: purchased, internally developed, and acquired in a business combination

front: State the governing rule for under IFRS, recoverable amount is the higher of value in use and:
back: fair value less costs of disposal. The higher of the two valuation bases is recoverable amount.

front: Resolve this long-term-asset review point: an impairment loss immediately lowers:

back: added back to net income in CFO. It reduced income without using cash.
